Food · Designs for testing

Five dishes, designed to be cooked at home first.

Chicken 65 from South India on thick masa totopos. Paneer tikka in a taco. A goat birria. A roasted gobi taco. A butter chicken quesadilla with roasted poblano. Nothing is cooked for guests and nothing is for sale.

Concept stage: there is no brewery, no restaurant, no truck and no menu for sale. Images are concept visualizations and illustrations, not photographs of NASHA. The pictures show proposed presentation, not finished dishes.

The Core 5

Five dishes, designed to be tested first.

Every card is a design. The pictures are generated concept images of how each dish is meant to look. Nothing here has been cooked for guests, and the founder's first real photographs will replace them.

Chicken 65 Totopos

IN DEVELOPMENT Proposed presentation · not cooked or tested

Bite-sized fried boneless chicken thigh in the style of South Indian Chicken 65, served on and with thick fried corn chips. It is a design in development and has not been cooked.

The chip becomes the plate, so chicken and chip are built to be eaten together. It is a shareable, hands-on opener that shows the Indo-Mex idea immediately.

The full design
Indian side
Chicken 65 with a yogurt, ginger, garlic and lemon marinade, curry leaf and green chile. It is associated with Chennai, but its origin is contested.
Mexican side
Fried nixtamal corn totopos as the base, with lime, onion and crema. The thick chip is NASHA's own design choice, not a Mexican standard.
How they join
The chicken and chip are eaten as one bite, with crema as an optional cooler in place of raita. Three constructions (integrated, ring, composed board) are planned for comparison.
Texture target
Crisp-shell juicy chicken; chip still crisp at ten minutes in
Cannot change without losing the dish
Boneless chicken thigh, rice flour and cornflour coating, curry leaf, green chile, fried corn tortilla wedges, lime.
Beer idea
Mexican-Style Lager (alternate: Pilsner)
Zero-proof idea
An agua-fresca-style drink of fruit, lime and a little salt: bright, acidic and lightly savory, served very cold.
Biggest kitchen risk
HIGH: moisture migration into chip; 10-minute failure test
Cultural care
Medium. The Chicken 65 origin and the Hyderabad or Andhra lineage are unconfirmed, so no single origin story should be told, and an advisor should review.
First test
A first home-kitchen test with the rules written beforehand: three ways of building the plate, scored blind at the start, after five minutes and after ten.

Paneer Tikka Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT Proposed presentation · not cooked or tested

A small corn-tortilla taco filled with charred, spiced paneer, green salsa, raw onion, cilantro and lime. It has not been cooked.

It gives vegetarian guests a hero dish rather than a side, and shows that tikka char and taco freshness fit naturally together.

The full design
Indian side
Paneer tikka: a thick hung-curd marinade, char and soft paneer. It comes from the North Indian and Punjabi restaurant tradition, and no inventor is documented.
Mexican side
Corn tortilla with salsa verde, onion, cilantro and lime; the taco form is Mexican-inspired. Optional charred pineapple is an echo of al pastor but is never called that.
How they join
Tandoor-style char on a taco, with salsa and lime doing the job that raita and chutney do beside tikka.
Texture target
Soft interior, visible char, crust that clings; tortilla does not tear
Cannot change without losing the dish
Paneer, hung-curd marinade with ginger, garlic, chile, kasuri methi and chaat masala, corn tortilla, salsa verde, onion, cilantro, lime.
Beer idea
Witbier (alternate: Mexican-Style Lager)
Zero-proof idea
A spiced-citrus drink with a gentle herbal edge and light sparkle that echoes lime and cilantro.
Biggest kitchen risk
MEDIUM-HIGH: paneer firms and dries, tortilla steams; finish to order
Cultural care
Medium. Pineapple is flagged as uncertain and needs advisor input, and the taco form and tikka are both borrowed, so both cultures should be credited plainly.
First test
A home test comparing heat sources for the char, with the marinade and the tortilla held the same.

Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise

IN DEVELOPMENT Proposed presentation · not cooked or tested

A slow braise of bone-in goat in a guajillo and ancho chile adobo, served as tacos with a small cup of consomme. It has not been cooked and is a long-lead item.

Birria de chivo is commonly made with goat in Jalisco (from web sources; an advisor is to confirm), and it lets NASHA make a rich, deep centrepiece that clearly reads as goat.

The full design
Indian side
Technique only: dum-style sealed-pot braising, whole-spice toasting and bhuna-style frying of the adobo paste. Yogurt-papaya and curry-leaf ideas are tested against a plain adobo, not assumed.
Mexican side
Goat, chile adobo, consomme, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime and salsa. These are historically supported from web sources, with a Mexican advisor still to confirm.
How they join
The Mexican dish stays whole, and the Indian layer is included only where tasting shows it adds depth. The dipped and griddled taco form is a modern adaptation.
Texture target
Tender but fibrous goat; drinkable consomme; tortilla holds after dipping
Cannot change without losing the dish
Bone-in goat, guajillo and ancho adobo, goat, chicken or vegetable stock only, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime.
Beer idea
Hefeweizen (alternate: Vienna Amber)
Zero-proof idea
A tea-based drink with tamarind or hibiscus acid and warm spice, served cool or slightly warm, matching the dish's chile and cinnamon notes.
Biggest kitchen risk
HIGH: large braise cooling/reheating/hold, fat set in consomme (food-safety professional must set the process)
Cultural care
Higher. Birria is a living Mexican regional dish, so Mexican advisor review is needed, and the sealed-pot link to India is a parallel rather than a shared origin.
First test
One small home braise: weigh the meat, the bone and the loss, and see whether it reads clearly as goat and what it really costs.

Gobi Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT Proposed presentation · not cooked or tested

A corn-tortilla taco with roasted cauliflower florets, a tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. It has not been cooked.

It is a vegetarian taco meant to stand on its own, with the cauliflower recognisable and not hidden under batter.

The full design
Indian side
Inspired by Gobi 65 and tandoori gobi. Gobi Manchurian is Indo-Chinese and is only named if actually used.
Mexican side
Corn tortilla, lime-cabbage slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. No traditional Mexican cauliflower taco is claimed.
How they join
Roast-first cauliflower with a late tamarind and guajillo glaze, so slaw and pickle add the acid and crunch. A batter-fried version is a comparison, and fry versus roast is still undecided.
Texture target
Visible florets with dark tips and cream stems; crunch retained 10 min
Cannot change without losing the dish
Cauliflower florets, tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, corn tortilla, pickled onion, cilantro.
Beer idea
Pilsner (alternate: Mexican-Style Lager)
Zero-proof idea
A lime-forward agua-fresca-style drink with a pinch of salt and a little green herb, cold and crisp.
Biggest kitchen risk
MEDIUM-HIGH: cauliflower keeps releasing water; glaze and slaw soften crust
Cultural care
Lower to medium. The glaze is an original house idea with no claimed precedent, and the dish should be called modern fusion and not traditional.
First test
A home test of roasting against frying, scored for how long the crunch lasts.

Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla

IN DEVELOPMENT Proposed presentation · not cooked or tested

A griddled quesadilla filled with reduced butter chicken, charred chicken, melting cheese and roasted poblano strips. It has not been cooked.

It takes one of the best-known Indian comfort dishes and puts it in a handheld, shareable Mexican form.

The full design
Indian side
Murgh makhani: a tomato, butter and cream gravy with kasuri methi and tandoori-style charred chicken. Its origin is contested in court, so we do not pick a side.
Mexican side
Quesadilla con rajas: roasted poblano strips and Oaxaca-style cheese, griddled on a comal.
How they join
The makhani is reduced until clingy so it stays inside, and poblano smoke and acid balance the richness. A dip is optional and served separately.
Texture target
Crisp-browned tortilla, set filling, melted cheese fused, no leak
Cannot change without losing the dish
Chicken thigh, reduced makhani, roasted poblano rajas, Oaxaca-style cheese, tortilla, kasuri methi.
Beer idea
Vienna Amber (alternate: Hefeweizen)
Zero-proof idea
A lassi-inspired drink of cultured dairy, fruit and a little spice, served cold, to echo the sauce and cool the richness.
Biggest kitchen risk
MEDIUM: steams soft if covered; filling leaks if sauce not reduced
Cultural care
Medium. The dish's origin is disputed, so we should tell no single origin story, and the quesadilla con rajas is borrowed from Mexican home cooking and should be credited.
First test
A home test of filling weight and griddle time, to see how it holds together and how fast it cooks.

Vegetarian is not a side.

Two of the five are vegetarian as designed, built as headliners. Every dish is made without beef or pork, including stocks, fats and tortillas.

Labels describe design intent, not a certified dietary or allergen statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. See the pairings for what each dish is meant to meet; the pairings are proposed and not sensory tested.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development. Nothing is open or for sale, and no site has been chosen. Pictures are concept visualizations or drawings, not photographs of NASHA.

Name, images and allergens

The name was chosen by the founder; legal clearance is pending and nothing here claims trademark ownership. The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, not a logo. Nasha means intoxication or addiction in Hindi and Urdu: we chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company, we will never present excess as something to admire, and cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited; drawings are illustrations. None is a photograph of NASHA, its food or its beer (about these images). Dishes are designs for testing, not served food; heat and vegetarian labels are design intent, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly; alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.
